_comment: HARPS-tuned regular Cartesian grid example for interpolation-ready datasets.
_harps: HARPS = High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher, the fibre-fed echelle spectrograph on the ESO 3.6 m at La Silla.
Resolving power R ~ 115000 -> turbospectrum.overrides.synthesis_parameters.resolution = 115000.0 convolves output to the instrument profile.
Wavelength coverage 3780-6910 A across two CCDs, with a physical gap at ~5304-5337 A (between the blue and red detectors).

CCD GAP NOTE: this pipeline writes a single contiguous LAMBDA_MIN/MAX/STEP window to bsyn (run_turbospectrum.py); segments_file is NOT wired through the Python wrapper. For detector-faithful spectra, either mask 5304-5337 A downstream, or run two passes - blue CCD lam_min/lam_max = 3780/5304 and red CCD = 5337/6910 - and concatenate.
lam_step = 0.01 A gives ~4 points per resolution element at 5000 A (FWHM ~ 0.043 A); the full window is ~313k wavelength points per spectrum.
The axes below form a coarse FGK Cartesian grid (5 x 4 x 4 x 2 = 160 points) suitable for linear interpolation; refine the step syntax for a denser grid.
_note: For HPC, use turbospectrum_pipeline_example.pbs (the single script for LHS and regular grids) which reads output/runtime paths from this config by default.
Set runtime.rows_per_shard (or runtime.shard_count) to switch from one-row shards to chunked shards for array jobs and lower startup overhead.
When synthesized, turbvel is preserved as a numeric parameter column alongside vmicro in the final spectra Zarr.
Base synthesis runtime config used by synthesize_spectra_from_zarr.py.
overrides carries the HARPS resolution and linelist settings without duplicating the full synthesis schema.

outputs._note: run_root is resolved relative to this config unless absolute; output paths under outputs/... are resolved relative to run_root.

runtime._note: rows_per_shard is recommended for regular-grid HPC runs; PBS arrays can overshoot the final index because extra tasks exit cleanly.
